chunks: And in the narration of Abān ibn ʿUthmān:

That ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was brought a man who had killed another man's brother. So he handed him over to him and ordered him to kill him. The man struck him until he thought that he had killed him. Then he was carried to his home, and they found in him some remaining life, so they treated him until he recovered. When he came out, the brother of the first slain man seized him and said: “You are the killer of my brother, and I have the right to kill you.” He said to him: “You have already killed me once.” So he took him to ʿUmar, and he ordered that he be killed. Then he went out while saying: “O people, by Allah, he has already killed me once.” Then they passed by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ, and informed him of his case, so he said: “Do not hasten against him until I come out to you.”

Then he, peace be upon him, entered upon ʿUmar and said: “The ruling concerning him is not like this.” He said: “What is it, O Abā al-Ḥasan?” He said: “This one should exact retribution from the brother of the first slain man for what he did to him, then he should kill him for his brother.” So the man thought that if he exacted retribution from him, it would finish him off, so he pardoned him, and they let one another go.

key_terms.الْحُكْمُ: the legal ruling or judgment in the case
key_terms.الْمَقْتُولِ الْأَوَّلِ: the first slain person whose killing is the basis of the case
key_terms.فَعَفَا عَنْهُ: he pardoned him and waived retaliation
key_terms.يَقْتَصُّ: he exacts retaliation in equal measure

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام rule in a case where a murder convict survived an attempted execution?
ai.summary: This narration recounts a legal case in which Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام corrected an incorrect judgment regarding retaliation for murder. It highlights the principle of qiṣāṣ in a measured and reciprocal form, while also showing that pardon can end a dispute between the parties.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5401 - In the narration of Aban ibn Uthman,

it is reported that Umar ibn Al-Khattab was presented with a man who had killed another man's brother. Umar handed him over to the victim's brother and ordered him to kill him. The man struck him until he thought he had killed him. He was carried to his home, and they found he still had some life in him.
They treated him until he recovered. When he recovered, the brother of the first murdered man seized him and said:
"You are the killer of my brother, and I have the right to kill you."
The man replied: "You have already killed me once."
He was then brought before Umar, who ordered his execution.
As he was being taken away, he cried out:
"O' people, by Allah (swt), he has already killed me once!"
They passed by Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) and informed him of the situation.
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "Do not rush to kill him until I come out to you."

Imam (as) entered upon Umar and said: "This is not the correct ruling in this matter."
Umar asked: "Then what is it, O' Abu Al-Hasan (as)?"
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) replied: "This man should exact retribution from the brother of the first murdered man for what he did to him, and then he can be executed for his brother."
The man thought that if he took retribution, it would lead to his own death, so he pardoned him, and they both left each other in peace.
